title: The construction and validation of the Rula wellbeing scale.
abstract:
INRODUCTION: Psychotherapy outcome research has traditionally emphasized symptom reduction, yet psychotherapy may also enhance eudaimonic wellbeing, including meaning, purpose, connectedness, and adaptive functioning. Despite growing interest in wellbeing as a treatment outcome, few ultra-brief measures are available for routine use in psychotherapy. The present series of studies developed and evaluated the Rula Wellbeing Scale (RWS), a four-item measure designed to assess core domains of eudaimonic wellbeing relevant to clinical practice.
METHODS: In Study 1, exploratory factor analysis was used to refine an initial 12-item pool, resulting in a unidimensional four-item solution assessing social connectedness, daily functioning, purpose, and emotion regulation. In Study 2, confirmatory factor analysis in an independent non-clinical sample supported a single-factor structure, whereas a bifactor model was not supported. In both Study 1 & 2, the RWS demonstrated good internal consistency and expected associations with related constructs, including positive correlations with life satisfaction, flourishing, and global wellbeing, and a negative correlation with loneliness. In Study 3, the single-factor structure was replicated in a clinical sample of psychotherapy clients, and the scale demonstrated acceptable internal consistency.
RESULTS: As hypothesized, the RWS scores were negatively associated with depression and anxiety. Mean scores were also lower in the clinical sample than in the non-clinical sample, supporting sensitivity to differences in wellbeing across populations.
DISCUSSION: Collectively, findings provide initial support for the RWS as a psychometrically sound, ultra-brief measure of eudaimonic wellbeing. The scale may have particular utility in psychotherapy and measurement-based care contexts where brief, practical, and conceptually meaningful assessment tools are needed.
